query:
In the discussion of mono pressings versus fold-down stereo cuts, one member argues that listening will show you the difference even where measurements look clean. Who actually made that argument?

Options:
A. Bram
B. Marcy
C. Theo
D. Felix
context:
[1] (about=Theo, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:14:00) Bram is right. I would add: even where measurements are clean, the sound character of a mono cut still differs in ways the measurements undersell. in my view this is one place where listening leads.
[2] (about=Bram, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:11:00) good question Dev, both. mono uses a horizontal-only cutting head and a dedicated mono tape if one exists, fold-down is a stereo cut summed to mono playback. they sound different. the mono cut is louder and more present, the fold-down is just half a stereo. listening tests will show you, even without measurements.
[3] (about=Yuko, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:18:00) I would push back. The measurements undersell because the typical measurement set was designed for stereo. New measurement protocols catch what you describe. The conclusion is not that listening leads, it is that the measurement vocabulary needs updating.
[4] (about=Dev, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:08:00) lowkey question, what is the actual difference between a mono pressing and a fold-down stereo? I keep reading conflicting stuff and ngl I'm getting confused. is it the cutting head or the master tape or both??
[5] (about=Bram, episodic, t0 @2026-01-12T19:43:00) on the other hand both can be true. measurements set the floor, listening sets the ceiling. that's how I usually frame it for my students anyway. cheers.
[6] (about=Yuko, episodic, t16 @2026-03-09T18:10:00) Correct, and the recording venue is acoustically calibrated to within centimeters of the same coordinates session to session. The dataset is unusually controlled.
[7] (about=Yuko, episodic, t14 @2026-03-02T19:20:00) A measurement-based view: well-mastered hi-res digital at 24/96 is indistinguishable from a clean LP at the threshold of human hearing for most listeners. The remaining differences are in mastering and pressing variance. Hema's shift is technically sound.
[8] (about=Yuko, episodic, t8 @2026-02-09T19:41:00) A measurement-based view: typical conversational volume sits around 60 dB SPL at the listening position. Concert level is 85+ dB. The dynamic and tonal experience differs by an order of magnitude. The audiologist recommendation is sound.
[9] (about=Olin, episodic, t8 @2026-02-09T19:31:00) Lina, this is a meaningful shift; hearing compensation is an underdiscussed factor in mature listeners. The Beethoven 9 is the right reference. I would suggest the Furtwangler 1942 for the same exercise; the dynamic range is enormous.
[10] (about=Yuko, episodic, t4 @2026-01-26T19:46:00) Correct. The signal-to-noise floor of the listening room defines the perceived dynamic range. I see this every site visit.
agent_answer:
C. Theo

Theo said: "even where measurements are clean, the sound character of a mono cut still differs in ways the measurements undersell. in my view this is one place where listening leads."

Bram did say listening tests will show the difference, but phrased it as "even without measurements," not "even where measurements look clean."

query:
During the digital-vs-vinyl debrief, one member argues that well-mastered hi-res digital at 24/96 is indistinguishable from a clean LP for most listeners at the threshold of human hearing. Who made that argument?

Options:
A. Quint
B. Yuko
C. Theo
D. Sander
context:
[1] (about=Yuko, episodic, t14 @2026-03-02T19:20:00) A measurement-based view: well-mastered hi-res digital at 24/96 is indistinguishable from a clean LP at the threshold of human hearing for most listeners. The remaining differences are in mastering and pressing variance. Hema's shift is technically sound.
[2] (about=Marcy, episodic, t14 @2026-03-02T19:23:00) fwiw I have been making this argument for years. mastering and pressing variance dominate format differences once you get past 24/96. just my read, but the data is clear.
[3] (about=Theo, episodic, t10 @2026-02-16T19:22:00) well. fine. I will say it openly. that SACD was excellent. measurements aside, the harmonic structure and dynamic decay were uncannily close to a clean LP, and on a couple of tracks the SACD pulled ahead. I am not converting. but I will concede a well-mastered SACD can sit alongside vinyl. tube preamp and the right DAC and I can listen to it.
[4] (about=Theo, episodic, t10 @2026-02-16T19:28:00) Sander, you are correct, and I can hear my younger self being insufferable about it. in my view I was wrong about the ceiling on digital, but right about most of the digital that existed in 1998.
[5] (about=Sander, episodic, t10 @2026-02-16T19:25:00) knew this day would come. forum days you said digital was lifeless. circa 1998 you said it would never sound right. and here we are.
[6] (about=Hema, episodic, t13 @2026-03-02T19:08:00) An admission. The firm took on a digital archive commission for a regional symphony, and I have been working with their hi-res files daily for three months. The studio listening room has digital playback now. I still play vinyl at home. But I no longer dismiss digital as a serious format. The work changed my view.
[7] (about=Marcy, episodic, t16 @2026-03-09T18:18:00) fwiw on Olin's point, the Berlin Phil engineering team uses neural mastering at the post-production stage. it is an open methodological question whether the hi-res advantage is the recording or the algorithmic refinement. just my read.
[8] (about=Marcy, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:42:00) Olin, I do disagree, partially. The DG bass character was a tape-stage decision more than a pressing decision. The 2018 thinning is a transfer choice, not a mastering one. I won't argue Esoteric does the cleanest digital, just my read.
[9] (about=Olin, episodic, t16 @2026-03-09T18:04:00) Adding to the admissions; my daughter gave me a Berlin Phil Digital Concert Hall subscription for my birthday. Three weeks of streaming. The Bartok cycle they put up is technically and musically superior to the analog reissues I have been advocating for thirty years. I am revising my position. Hi-res streams from a serious orchestra archive can equal or beat reissued analog. I would not have written this in a column ten years ago.
[10] (about=Dev, episodic, t8 @2026-02-09T19:48:00) lol Bram. okay so I was wondering, how do you guys figure out which records hold up at higher volume?? is it mastering or pressing or both??
